title: Feels Like Yesterday
blurb: Apps, gadgets, athletes and hits from 2000 to 2025. Three facts, one cap, zero mercy.

cards.say: The iPod [only worked with Mac computers when it first came out], [got its name from a line in the movie 2001: A Space Odyssey], [was sold until 2022, almost 15 years after the first iPhone], and [could hold about 10,000 songs in its very first version].
cards.real: The first iPod, released in November 2001, had a 5 GB hard drive and was sold as 1,000 songs in your pocket.
src: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IPod (iPod software originally worked only with Mac; Windows support came with the second generation)
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IPod (Vinnie Chieco, inspired by Open the pod bay doors, Hal)
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IPod (iPod Touch discontinued May 10, 2022; the first iPhone went on sale in June 2007)
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IPod (first model, November 10, 2001: 5 GB, 1,000 songs in your pocket)

cards.say: Android [was first built to run digital cameras], [came out on its first phone before the iPhone did], [was bought by Google three years before the first Android phone], and [named its versions after desserts, in ABC order].
cards.real: The first Android phone, the T-Mobile G1, came out in October 2008, more than a year after the first iPhone in June 2007.
src: https://www.androidcentral.com/apps-software/android-os/the-evolution-of-android-decades-of-transformation + https://www.computerworld.com/article/1405537/android-founder-we-aimed-to-make-a-camera-os.html
https://www.androidcentral.com/apps-software/android-os/the-evolution-of-android-decades-of-transformation (HTC Dream / T-Mobile G1, October 2008)
https://www.androidcentral.com/apps-software/android-os/the-evolution-of-android-decades-of-transformation (Google acquired Android Inc. in July 2005)
https://www.slashgear.com/2196404/the-reason-why-android-stopped-using-dessert-names-for-new-versions/ (sweet treats in alphabetical order from Cupcake in 2009; dropped with Android 10 in 2019)

cards.say: Gmail [launched by giving every user 10 megabytes of free storage], [was announced on April Fools' Day, so many people thought it was a joke], [took nearly three years to open to everyone without an invite], and [was code-named Caribou after a Dilbert comic strip].
cards.real: Gmail launched in 2004 with 1 gigabyte per user, when most free email gave 2 to 4 megabytes. That's partly why people thought it was a prank.
src: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_Gmail (1 GB per account; the standard was 2 to 4 MB)
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_Gmail (announced April 1, 2004, met with skepticism)
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_Gmail (invitations no longer required from February 14, 2007)
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_Gmail (Project Caribou, a Dilbert reference)

cards.say: Duolingo [was co-founded by the inventor of reCAPTCHA], [has offered a course in Klingon, the language from Star Trek], [began as a project at Stanford University in California], and [was dreamed up in 2009 by a professor and his grad student].
cards.real: Duolingo started at Carnegie Mellon University in Pittsburgh, where professor Luis von Ahn and grad student Severin Hacker came up with it in 2009.
src: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_von_Ahn (in 2007 von Ahn invented reCAPTCHA; co-founded Duolingo with Severin Hacker)
https://www.engadget.com/2018/03/15/duolingos-klingon-language-course/ (Klingon course launched March 15, 2018)
https://keystoneedge.com/2015/12/31/founder-profile-luis-von-ahn/ (Duolingo is a CMU spinoff) + https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_von_Ahn (professor at Carnegie Mellon)
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_von_Ahn (in 2009 von Ahn, a CMU professor, and grad student Severin Hacker began developing Duolingo)

cards.say: Shazam [started in 2002 as a number you dialed while a song played], [texted you the song's name after the call], [was bought by Google in a 2018 deal worth 400 million dollars], and [was one of the first apps in Apple's App Store in 2008].
cards.real: It was Apple that bought Shazam, finishing the deal in September 2018 for a reported 400 million dollars.
src: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shazam_(music_app) (UK service launched 2002 as 2580, the number users dialed)
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shazam_(music_app) (a text message with the title and artist was sent back)
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shazam_(music_app) (Apple announced the purchase in December 2017 for a reported 400 million dollars; completed 24 September 2018)
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shazam_(music_app) (debuted on iPhone 10 July 2008 with the launch of the App Store)

cards.say: BTS [won a Grammy for its 2020 hit Dynamite], [has a name that means Bulletproof Boy Scouts in Korean], [spoke at the United Nations in 2018], and [became the first Korean group to top the US Hot 100].
cards.real: Dynamite made BTS the first K-pop group nominated for a Grammy, but the award went to Rain On Me by Lady Gaga and Ariana Grande.
src: https://learningenglish.voanews.com/amp/k-pop-band-bts-honored-to-receive-first-grammy-nomination/5807866.html (first K-pop group nominated) + https://www.koreajoongangdaily.com/entertainment/bts-fails-to-take-win-from-first-grammy-nomination/10156438 (Rain On Me won)
https://www.britannica.com/topic/BTS (Bangtan Sonyeondan, Bulletproof Boy Scouts)
https://www.unicef.org/press-releases/remarks-kim-nam-jun-launch-generation-unlimited-new-york-24-september-2018 (RM spoke at the UN General Assembly, 24 September 2018)

https://www.hawaiipublicradio.org/asia-minute/2020-11-26/asia-minute-south-koreas-grammy-triumph-follows-oscar-win (first Korean group to top the Billboard Hot 100) + https://www.britannica.com/topic/BTS (Dynamite debuted at number one)

cards.say: LeBron James [was on the cover of Sports Illustrated while still in high school], [had one of his high school games shown on national TV], [played in an NBA game alongside his own son in 2024], and [scored 31 points in his very first game in the NBA].
cards.real: LeBron scored 25 points in his first NBA game, a 106 to 92 loss to the Sacramento Kings. He had gone first in the 2003 draft, straight from high school.
src: https://www.si.com/high-school/national/2022/08/30/lebron-james-court-sons-bronny-bryce-flank-the-king-on-sports-illustrated-cover (first on the SI cover in 2002 at St. Vincent-St. Mary High School) + https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LeBron_James
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LeBron_James (the December 12, 2002 game against Oak Hill Academy was nationally televised on ESPN2)
https://www.guinnessworldrecords.com/world-records/770480-first-father-son-duo-to-play-on-the-same-nba-team-at-the-same-time (with Bronny on 22 October 2024)
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LeBron_James (25 points in a 106 to 92 debut loss to the Sacramento Kings; first pick of the 2003 draft, prep-to-pro)

cards.say: Stephen Curry [was born in the very same Ohio hospital as LeBron James], [was the first overall pick in the 2009 NBA draft], [was offered only a walk-on spot by his dad's old college], and [became the NBA's first unanimous MVP in 2016].
cards.real: Curry went seventh in the 2009 NBA draft, picked by the Golden State Warriors.
src: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Curry (born at Summa Health Akron Campus, Akron, Ohio) + https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LeBron_James (born at Summa Health Akron Campus, Akron, Ohio)

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Curry (Virginia Tech, where his father had a storied career, offered only a walk-on spot)
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Curry (first unanimous MVP, 2015-16 season)

cards.say: Serena Williams [turned pro at just 14 years old], [won her 23rd and final Grand Slam title while pregnant], [won her first Grand Slam singles title at Wimbledon in 1999], and [won four Olympic golds, three of them with her sister Venus].
cards.real: Serena's first Grand Slam singles title came at the 1999 US Open. Her first Wimbledon title came three years later, in 2002.
src: https://wtatennis.com/serena-career-timeline/1995-2022 (pro debut at 14 in Quebec City, 1995)
https://wtatennis.com/serena-career-timeline/1995-2022 (2017 Australian Open, while pregnant)
https://wtatennis.com/serena-career-timeline/1995-2022 (first Slam at the 1999 US Open; first Wimbledon title 2002)
https://wtatennis.com/serena-career-timeline/1995-2022 (singles gold 2012; doubles gold with Venus 2000, 2008, 2012)

cards.say: Roger Federer [won an Olympic gold medal in men's singles at London 2012], [was a ball boy at the Basel tournament he later won 10 times], [was the first living person honored on a Swiss coin], and [holds both Swiss and South African citizenship].
cards.real: Federer's Olympic gold came in doubles, with Stan Wawrinka in 2008. At London 2012 he took silver in singles, losing the final to Andy Murray.
src: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Federer (doubles gold with Stan Wawrinka in 2008; singles silver in London 2012, losing the final to Andy Murray)

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Federer (ball boy at the Swiss Indoors in Basel in 1992 and 1993) + https://www.skysports.com/tennis/news/12110/11846691/roger-federer-claims-historic-10th-title-at-swiss-indoors-basel (10th title, October 2019)
https://www.tennis.com/baseline/articles/federer-to-be-minted-on-20-franc-silver-coin-in-switzerland (first living person in Switzerland honored with a Swissmint commemorative coin)
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Federer (his mother is South African; he holds both Swiss and South African citizenship)

cards.say: Lionel Messi [had his first Barcelona deal written on a paper napkin at 13], [saw that napkin sell at auction for nearly a million dollars in 2024], [left Barcelona in 2021 with a club-record 672 goals], and [was born in Argentina's capital city, Buenos Aires].
cards.real: Messi was born in Rosario, a city northwest of Buenos Aires, and moved to Barcelona as a 13-year-old.
src: https://www.kuow.org/stories/napkin-securing-lionel-messi-s-first-contract-fetches-nearly-1-million-at-auction (napkin dated Dec. 14, 2000; Messi was 13)

https://www.kuow.org/stories/napkin-securing-lionel-messi-s-first-contract-fetches-nearly-1-million-at-auction (club-record 672 goals in 778 games; joined Paris Saint-Germain in 2021)

https://www.britannica.com/summary/Lionel-Messi (born June 24, 1987, Rosario, Argentina) + https://wtop.com/funny-weird-news/2024/05/messi-napkin-that-sealed-barcelona-move-sells-for-965000-at-auction (moved to Barcelona at 13)

cards.say: Shohei Ohtani [became MLB's first 50-homer, 50-steal player in 2024], [started his pro career with the Los Angeles Dodgers], [signed a 700 million dollar deal, then the biggest in sports], and [had his dog Decoy deliver a ceremonial first pitch].
cards.real: Ohtani turned pro in Japan with the Nippon-Ham Fighters, who drafted him in 2012. He signed with the Angels in 2017 and with the Dodgers after the 2023 season.
src: https://britannica.com/biography/Shohei-Ohtani (54 homers, 59 steals in 2024) + https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/50%E2%80%9350_club_(baseball)
